countermodel: F(x)=x^(4/5)*sin(log x)^2, x>=1. F is C^1, nonnegative, and |F'(x)| <= 9/5 for all x>=1. Zeros Y_k=exp(k*pi) are unbounded, so F(Y_k)<=Y_k^theta for every k. But x_k=exp((k+1/2)*pi) lies inside [Y_k,Y_k^(3/2)] for all k>=1, and F(x_k)/x_k^theta=exp((1/5)*(k+1/2)*pi)->infinity. Thus single good scales, even under global bounded derivative, cannot replace full windows. This is a toy function, not the prime-power statistic G(x).
uniform_constant_countermodel: F(x)=x^(4/5): for each x there is C_x=x^(1/5) with F(x)<=C_x*x^(3/5), but there is no x-independent C. Thus the fixed K in H12 is a substantive quantifier.
scope: Quantifier logic of the human guide III.11, not an objection to Alpoge Lean theorem, which asserts full H12-type hypotheses within the formal proof.
